slice.leaf: test Certificate Transparency v2 as a different externally queryable monotonic/permanence witness family
slice.hypothesis: An RFC-defined transparency log can provide a stronger durable ordering witness than undocumented repository-number allocation because append-only evolution is explicitly verifiable rather than inferred from allocator behavior.

public_source.title: RFC 9162: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0
sections_used: 5.3 Retrieve Merkle Consistency Proof between Two STHs

observations: RFC 9162 explicitly defines each log as a single append-only Merkle Tree and states that Merkle consistency proofs prove the append-only property between earlier and later tree heads.

The protocol defines signed tree heads and a latest-STH retrieval endpoint plus a consistency-proof endpoint, so the monotonic relation is externally checkable at the protocol level rather than relying on undocumented allocator behavior.
The RFC also warns that a misbehaving log can present inconsistent split views; therefore a single-source observation is not by itself a global non-equivocation guarantee.
slice.falsification_or_limit: This slice did not verify a currently live public CT v2 endpoint, its no-account/no-monthly-quota access terms, or cross-view gossip/non-equivocation from scheduled Chat. Therefore the family is not yet Phase-1 acceptance evidence.

comparison_assumptions.prior_own_leaf: Repository issue/PR numbering was rejected for certification because official documentation did not state monotonic non-reuse semantics.
comparison_assumptions.ct_advantage: RFC 9162 supplies explicit append-only and consistency-proof semantics.
comparison_assumptions.ct_remaining_risk: Operational availability, zero-optional-quota access, operator liveness, and split-view resistance remain separate children.
